stemMd: An object $2.0\ \text{cm}$ tall stands upright on the axis of a thin converging lens of focal length $10\ \text{cm}$, at a distance of $15\ \text{cm}$ from the lens. What is the height of the image formed by the lens?
explanationMd:
**Method.** Find the image distance $q$ with the thin-lens equation $\dfrac1p+\dfrac1q=\dfrac1f$, then the magnification $\dfrac{q}{p}$.

**The computation.**

$$\frac1q=\frac1{10}-\frac1{15}=\frac{3-2}{30}=\frac1{30}\quad\Rightarrow\quad q=30\ \text{cm}.$$

The magnification is $\dfrac{q}{p}=\dfrac{30}{15}=2$, so the image is $2\cdot 2.0=4.0\ \text{cm}$ tall (real and inverted).

**How to check it.** An object between $f$ and $2f$ always gives a real image beyond $2f$ that is larger than the object. Here $10<15<20$ and $q=30>20$, and the image is indeed enlarged.

distractorRationale.e: Inverts the magnification, using $\tfrac{p}{q}=\tfrac12$ instead of $\tfrac{q}{p}$, and so shrinks the image.
distractorRationale.d: Adds the reciprocals, $\tfrac1q=\tfrac1{10}+\tfrac1{15}=\tfrac16$, getting $q=6\ \text{cm}$ and a magnification of $0.4$.
distractorRationale.b: Uses $\tfrac{q}{f}=3$ as the magnification instead of $\tfrac{q}{p}$.
distractorRationale.a: Takes the image distance as $p-f=5\ \text{cm}$ instead of using the lens equation, giving a magnification of $\tfrac13$.

accessibilityText: An object 2.0 centimetres tall stands on the axis of a thin converging lens of focal length 10 centimetres, 15 centimetres from the lens. Find the height of the image. The five choices are: two thirds of a centimetre; 6.0 centimetres; 4.0 centimetres; 0.80 centimetres; 1.0 centimetre.

provenance.notes: Original item on the thin-lens equation and magnification for an object between f and 2f. Distractors: inverted magnification, added reciprocals, magnification relative to f, and a subtraction shortcut.

independentSolve.workingNotes: 1/q=1/10-1/15=1/30 gives q=30 cm, magnification -q/p=-2, image height 4.0 cm (real, inverted). 6.0 cm is 1/q added wrongly (q=6); 2/3, 0.80, 1.0 cm come from other formula slips. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolcf-mpl-run1) reached the same answer: 1/q = 1/10 - 1/15 = 1/30, so q=30 cm, |m|=30/15=2, so the image height is 4.0 cm (real, inverted). 2/3 cm and 1.0 cm invert the magnification; 6.0 cm uses q/f.]
